newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Villagers give evidence in Sri Lanka massacre case.
newsitem.headline: Villagers give evidence in Sri Lanka massacre case.

text.p: A labourer from Sri Lanka's minority Tamil community told a court how he saw bullets rake the thatched walls of his house as government soldiers stood outside firing, court officials said on Thursday.

Krishnan Palanivel, 30, whose father was among 25 people killed in a massacre of Tamil villagers in eastern Sri Lanka last year, was giving evidence on Wednesday against eight soldiers charged with the atrocity, officials said.

Women and children were among the dead in the attack on the village of Kumarapuram, 30 km (19 miles) from the eastern port town of Trincomalee, on February 11, 1996. Trincomalee is 240 km (150 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo.
The soldiers have also been charged with the attempted murder of 26 civilians wounded in the attack.
Seven witnesses, out of a total of 120, gave evidence when the hearing resumed on Wednesday at a magistrate's court in eastern Muttur.
Palanivel told court how, upon returning home from work that evening, he saw two persons in army uniform standing outside his house and firing.
Bullets smashed the walls, which were made from coconut thatch, he said. Palanivel said he later found the bullet-riddled body of his father inside.
He identified two suspects as the people who had fired at his house.
A 27-year-old mother of three, Pakyarasa Purnam, told the court that she hid inside a shop with her children and husband after hearing gunfire.

Two men dressed in army uniforms came to the shop and began shooting. Her husband was killed, but she managed to run away from the back door with the children, she said. She could not identify any of the suspects.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, had killed two soldiers near Kumarapuram the same day.
The government ordered an inquiry into the massacre after complaints by Tamil members of parliament.
The inquiry was deferred to June 11.
Human rights groups have accused Sri Lankan security forces of rights abuses during operations against the LTTE.
The international human rights group Amnesty International in April said more than 600 people were reported to have disappeared in the north during the past year, the highest number in five years.
The government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
